name: Animation and motion graphics
one_line: Designed moving-image work organised by storyboard, animation/compositing, review, render, and delivery rather than camera capture.

deterministic: A project/composition file has a timeline, named layers or precompositions, keyframes, vector/text shapes, and render configuration.
A storyboard or animatic has ordered panels/shots, timing annotations, transition notes, and a matching brief or script.
A review packet has a dated proof, annotated notes, and explicit timing, easing, typography, shot, or compositing revisions.
A render/delivery set has platform, aspect-ratio, codec, resolution, subtitle, or size variants plus a manifest for one work.
A project references imported vector artwork, fonts, audio, plates, or 3D renders by named paths or asset IDs.
needs_llm: whether moving image is authored animation, live-action post-production, a template modification, or a downloaded reference
the work and lifecycle stage when names say Untitled, Comp 01, v07, or Final
whether a delivery package is one work with variants or unrelated clips from a download session
whether a motion-identity deliverable is a brand system or client engagement member
whether an animatic, style frame, or storyboard is also a research, portfolio, or presentation artifact
never_alone: animation, motion, kinetic, title, explainer, reel, render, comp, storyboard, final, or delivery as words
a timeline screenshot, keyframe icon, motion blur, animated GIF, or high frame rate
a studio, agency, client, brand, campaign, performer, or software name without role-bearing project evidence
a version token, review date, output resolution, or missing EXIF
an .mp4/.mov without evidence; it may be camera footage, lecture, phone video, or reference
a bounded download session of fonts, templates, stock clips, LUTs, and presets

grouping_reasons: one work across brief, storyboard, source assets, project files, proofs, renders, and delivery variants
one review round linking proof, change notes, and subsequent render
one delivery set differing by platform, aspect ratio, codec, language, or resolution
one project file and linked media, vector layers, fonts, audio, or proxies
one client commission across motion deliverables and approval/handoff records

template.why: Creative is a field-less launch placeholder, so no folder dimension can be emitted. This template earns its node through a lifecycle signal distinct from the default creative making record: storyboard/treatment -> animation/compositing -> review -> render -> delivery, with linked assets and variant sets. If shared creative fields are later adopted, the likely recommendation is client only when it is not a one-child collector, then project, stage, and artifact_type. These are shared fields and lifecycle values, not new fields or child schemas; the order is a recommendation, not a path.

observations: ordered panels label shots and timing
notes identify narration, transitions, and revision date
must_not_conclude: client ownership from brand name alone

observations: rough timed panels combine temporary voiceover and shot changes
composition has named scenes, text layers, keyframes, precomps, linked SVGs, and output modules
annotated proof notes specify timing, easing, copy, and transitions
notes refer to preceding review export
render has square and vertical variants sharing a stem
metadata supplies dimensions, duration, and codec
rows list platform, aspect ratio, filename, subtitle language, checksum, and handoff status
manifest lists vector parts, rigs, textures, font references, audio, and proxy renders
template has editable text controls and animation presets
no brief, storyboard, review packet, or local work identity
camera filename and capture metadata identify an original clip
no animation project, keyframes, storyboard, or render set
public examples with source URLs and commentary
no local brief, source, review evidence, or authored render

collides_with.signal: Both have timelines, compositing, review exports, and rendered video; designed motion has keyframes, vector/text animation, generated scenes, and storyboard-to-render evidence, while post-production is anchored by recorded source footage.
Both have MOV/MP4; camera-original naming and capture metadata belong to shoot-day media, while renders and animation compositions belong here.
Both may contain Lottie, SVG, JSON, or scripts; repository/package/test structure is code evidence, while this node is the authored visual production.
Both may contain still style frames or screenshots; EXIF/capture-event evidence supports photos, while style frames need storyboard, composition, review, or render linkage.

falls_through_to.why: A storyboard, review note, or manifest without evidence of one accepted motion work remains standalone.
An ambiguous project file, detached render, unsupported file, or incomplete packet needs review.
Downloaded tutorials, public references, and template documentation are reference material.
An isolated style frame, poster, or thumbnail without production linkage is an image.

sensitivity_why: Unreleased concepts, client notes, source assets, licensed fonts/footage, voice tracks, and delivery variants may expose confidential work or third-party rights. The posture follows the packet, not the extension.
open_question: NJ-MOTION-1: Should future creative fields project/stage/artifact_type make this a destination template, or should motion remain structural on the field-less placeholder? Option A enables retrieval; Option B avoids premature fields. NJ-MOTION-2: Where a motion project composites substantial camera-original footage, should it co-activate creative.post-production, or should one template own the group while the other remains a collision boundary?
